lead: How ASNT certification works: employer-based certification under SNT-TC-1A and CP-189, and the central credentials ASNT examines and issues itself, ASNT NDT Level II, ASNT NDT Level III and ASNT 9712. answer.q: How do you get ASNT certified?
answer.a: There are two routes. Under SNT-TC-1A or CP-189, your employer certifies you against its written practice once your training hours, experience hours, vision examinations and general, specific and practical examinations are complete. ASNT's central credentials, ASNT NDT Level II, ASNT NDT Level III and ASNT 9712, are examined and issued by ASNT itself.

Level II: a further {l2Class} classroom hours and {l2Exp} hours of experience in the method
ASNT NDT Level III: the NDT Basic exam plus at least one method exam, after {l3Months} months of NDT experience depending on education

notes: ANSI/ASNT CP-189 (2024) is the ASNT standard for employer-based certification. It builds on SNT-TC-1A with fixed minimum requirements, and it requires Level III personnel to hold ASNT NDT Level III certification.

ACCP is a former programme name. ASNT states that the ASNT 9712 Certification Program replaced the ASNT Central Certification Program (ACCP), and its current programme list names ASNT NDT Level II, ASNT NDT Level III and ASNT 9712.

level2.h2: What does ASNT NDT Level II involve?
level2.p: For ASNT NDT Level II, ASNT administers a computer-based general exam and specific exams, currently in MT, PT, RT, UT and VT. ASNT states that employers are responsible for carrying out the visual acuity, practical and any job-specific exams. The credential is renewed every five years, by application with continued employment or by examination.
link: ASNT NDT Level II exam prep

level3.h2: What does ASNT NDT Level III require?
level3.intro: ASNT NDT Level III is ASNT's central Level III certification. First-time applicants pass the NDT Basic exam and at least one method exam; the exams are multiple-choice and computer-based. Experience must be in NDT, under qualified supervision, in the methods applied for.

faqs.a: ASNT certification can mean two things. Most NDT technicians are certified by their employer under ASNT Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1A or the ANSI/ASNT CP-189 standard, and ASNT does not issue those certificates. ASNT also runs its own central certifications, ASNT NDT Level II, ASNT NDT Level III and ASNT 9712, which it examines and issues to the individual.

faqs.q: What is the difference between SNT-TC-1A and ASNT 9712?
faqs.a: SNT-TC-1A is employer-based: your employer certifies you under its written practice, and the certification ends when you leave that employer. ASNT 9712 is a third-party programme designed to meet ISO 9712:2021. ASNT examines you, including practical exams, and issues a certificate that stays with you. ASNT says ASNT 9712 replaced the former ASNT Central Certification Program (ACCP).

faqs.q: How much does ASNT certification cost?
faqs.a: ASNT charges a fee per examination, with lower rates for ASNT members. The fee tables on this page list the figures ASNT published, checked in October 2026, and the ASNT certification pages carry the current schedule. Training is priced separately by each provider; ASNT does not set training fees.

faqs.q: How long does ASNT certification take?
faqs.a: The experience hours set the pace. SNT-TC-1A recommends {l1Exp} hours of experience in the method for Level I and a further {l2Exp} for Level II, depending on the method, alongside classroom training. ASNT NDT Level III needs {l3Months} months of NDT experience depending on education, plus the NDT Basic exam and a method exam.

faqs.q: What is the ASNT Level III exam format?
faqs.a: ASNT NDT Level III requires the NDT Basic exam, {exam.basic}, and at least one method exam: {exam.long} for UT, RT and ET, or {exam.short} for MT, PT and VT. The exams are multiple-choice and computer-based. Any specific examination on your employer's codes and procedures is set by its written practice, not by ASNT.

faqs.q: Do I need a degree for ASNT NDT Level III?
faqs.a: No. ASNT NDT Level III accepts candidates without college. A four-year degree, or two full academic years of engineering or physical science study, reduces the NDT experience required; the eligibility table on this page lists the minimums ASNT publishes.

faqs.q: Can I get ASNT certified online?
faqs.a: Theory training can be completed online, and the ASNT NDT Level III exams are computer-based. Practical examinations need hands-on work with real equipment: under SNT-TC-1A the employer gives them, and for ASNT NDT Level II ASNT states that employers carry out the practical exams. Atlantis delivers theory online and supervises practical training at the employer's facility.

ASNT describes its central certifications as internationally recognised, but the scheme a job needs is set by the contract or client specification. Some specifications, particularly in Europe, name ISO 9712 or PCN instead, and ASNT 9712 is the ASNT programme designed to meet ISO 9712:2021. Check the specification before choosing a route.

faqs.q: Does an Atlantis course certify me?
faqs.a: No. A course provides classroom training hours and a training record. Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after verifying your training and experience and giving the examinations its written practice requires. ASNT certifies only through its own examinations.

faqs.q: What does an NDT technician earn?
faqs.a: O*NET lists a median wage of $78,350 a year for Non-Destructive Testing Specialists (17-3029.01). The figure uses BLS data for the broader Engineering Technologists and Technicians, Except Drafters, All Other group, so treat it as an indication rather than a figure for a specific level.
